scores.evidence: Phase 1: Compliance; Phase 2: Cloud Foundation; Phase 3: Data Copying; Phase 4: Integrations; Phase 5: Testing; Phase 6: Cutover
scores.rationale: Ordering runs discovery, governance, foundation, data, integrations, test and cutover, which is sensible, but nothing is explicitly proven before the next phase starts and testing comes after integrations.
Phase 0 is only discovery, and no thin end-to-end slice runs in production before the full cutover.

scores.evidence: Truly zero write pause is only possible if the application was built for it. Plan for near-zero
scores.rationale: The plan makes some key decisions explicit (brief write pause, as-is move, rollback window, site phasing), but it has no consolidated list of irreversible decisions with defaults and flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Map every integration. This is usually where the risk is
scores.rationale: Some risk-first ordering appears, such as vendor confirmation first and read-only traffic before writes, but blast-radius ordering is not stated within phases.

scores.evidence: Sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with the cloud provider
scores.rationale: Security is covered in Phases 1, 2 and 5, but Phase 0 and the data and integration phases get little concrete security treatment, and the pen test comes late.

scores.evidence: Check continuously: row counts, checksums on key tables (appointments, slots, resources, patients), and replication lag.
scores.rationale: Monitoring and central logging appear in Phase 2, and replication and cutover monitoring appear later, but there is nothing in Phase 0 and no per-phase treatment.

scores.evidence: Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Bicep, etc.) so environments can be rebuilt the same way every time.
scores.rationale: Infrastructure as code and staging rehearsals are mentioned, but reproducibility is not threaded across phases.

scores.evidence: Failure testing: lose an availability zone, lose the connectivity link, and confirm replication recovers.
scores.rationale: Resilience appears in Phases 2, 3 (reverse replication), 5, 6 and 7, but it is absent from the early phases and failure testing is late.
The plan never states whether an AI layer applies, so the N/A declaration is missing.

scores.evidence: Don't redesign the app as part of this migration; that adds risk.
scores.rationale: The plan has a brief no-redesign note but no explicit deferred-work list and no pull-forward conditions.

note: The plan is a competent, practical migration with a good cutover and rollback design, but it is missing a walking skeleton, a decision-gate list, deferred-work tracking, and the explicit AI N/A statement.
